Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Binod Kumar Dwivedi

On The 9 th Of April, 2025
 Criminal Appeal No. 2818 of 2025
 Wasim Akaram Shah
 Versus
 The State Of Madhya Pradesh And Others
 Appearance:
 Shri Mitesh Jain - Advocate for the appellant.
 Shri Surendra Kumar Gupta - Govt. Advocate for the res
 State.
 Shri Kushal Patidar - Advocate for objector.

Order 
This first bail application in the form of criminal appeal under Section 14A (2) of Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 has been filed by the appellant Wasim Akram Shah S/o Teju Sham Muslim for grant of regular bail, who has been arrested on 18/03/2024 in connection with Crime No.125/2024 registered at Police Station Khachrod, District Ujjain (M.P.)
for commission of offences under Section 3(1)(R), 3(1) (S), 3(1)(W)(I), 3(1)(W)(II), 3(2)(V) and 3(2)(Va) of of SC/ST Act and Section 376, 376(2)(N), 376(D), 294, 201, 506, 450, 323, 384 and 377 of Indian Penal Code, 1860.

sentences.text: 2. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the appellant is innocent and has falsely been implicated in the crime.
Sufficient evidence is NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:9728 2 CRA-2818-2025 not available on record to establish the complicity of the accused with the alleged crime.
He further submits that this is a case of consensual relationship between appellant and victim, who is major.
No DNA report has been obtained to develop his case.
Learned counsel invited attention of this court towards para 2, 10, 20 to 24, 29 and 32 of the statement of the complainant.

Learned counsel further submits that co-accused Muzaffar Khan has been granted bail by this Court vide order dated 01/03/2025 passed in Criminal Appeal No.191/2025 as victim has already admitted in her cross- examination that in case he has paid the money, FIR might not have been lodged against Muzaffar.
He is suffering jail incarceration since 18/03/2024.
Investigation is complete and charge sheet has been filed.
He will abide by all the terms and conditions imposed by this Court.
There is no likelihood of his absconsion leaving his family, home and profession and also there is no likelihood of tampering with evidence by appellant.

sentences.text: 1 considerable long time, therefore, learned counsel prays for allowing the appeal and for grant of bail.

3. Learned counsel for the objector has vehemently opposed the appeal and invited attention of this Court towards para 34 of cross-examination of the victim and submits that all the accused persons have committed rape, which comes under the category of gang rape and have threatened the victim that her video and photographs will be made public and offence will also be committed with her daughter, therefore, prays for dismissal of the appeal.

4. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent / State has also vehemently opposed the prayer and prays for dismissal of the appeal inviting NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:9728 3 CRA-2818-2025 attention of this Court towards para 2 and 3 of the statement of victim.
He also submits that this is a case of gang rape, which has been committed upon the victim for considerable time in duress.

Hence, appellant is not entitled for bail.
5.
Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.
6. In the aforesaid factual backdrop, looking to the evidence in entirety, this Court is not inclined to grant benefit of bail to the appellant, who is main accused and the person behind this crime.
Accordingly, without commenting on the merits of the case, the appeal is dismissed.
Certified copy as per rules.
